title: Pair passing
description: Four cones per pair of players — two cones per player, spaced a few steps apart so each player can shuffle side to side within their own pair. The two players stand facing each other across a passing gap between their cone-pairs, shifting left and right with the ball and exchanging passes with their partner across the gap.
setup: Set two cones per player, spaced for a comfortable side-to-side shuffle. Pair players facing each other with a passing gap of about 5 yards between the two cone-pairs to start; adjust per session.

progressions.title: Clean control and pass
progressions.note: Take a good first touch to control the ball before passing it back across the gap — quality of the touch is the focus, not speed.

progressions.title: Right foot only
progressions.note: Repeat the same control-and-pass using only the right foot.

progressions.title: Left foot only
progressions.note: Repeat the same control-and-pass using only the left foot.

progressions.title: Open body receiving
progressions.note: Open the body side-on to receive, so the first touch sets the ball toward the next pass instead of straight back.

progressions.title: One-touch pass
progressions.note: Reduce to one touch — pass the ball back first-time, no separate controlling touch.

progressions.title: Pass and shuffle
progressions.note: After passing, shuffle to your other cone before receiving the return, so no one receives standing still.

progressions.title: Pass count challenge
progressions.note: Count clean passes completed as a pair in 90 seconds; try to beat the pair's count from the previous week.

progressions.title: Extended distance
progressions.note: Widen the gap between the two players so the pass travels farther and must be controlled with more pace.
